blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The country’s usual economic centers did not lead Philippine growth last year, with government data showing that some of the fastest-growing economies were in the Visayas and Mindanao. Dr. Alicor Panao, a data scientist for the Inquirer, said Western Visayas topped all regions with 6.38% real growth, followed by Caraga and the Negros Island Region at 5.70%, and the Davao Region at 5.15%. At the provincial level, Occidental Mindoro posted 11.16% growth, while General Santos, at 8.04%, and Cagayan de Oro City, at 7.37%, were among the fastest-growing highly urbanized cities.
